title: What a person of steady wisdom is like

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचस्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव । स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Kesava, what are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in stillness? How does a person of steady understanding speak, sit, and walk?
verses.angle: How does a steady man speak, sit, and walk
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the still mind. Now Arjuna asks how to recognize such a person in daily life.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Kesava, what are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in stillness? How does a person of steady understanding speak, sit, and walk? Arjuna asks a practical question, how does a steady man speak, sit, and walk, and Krishna answers by saying he is satisfied in the true self, a state where no desire remains. Krishna names this person steady in wisdom, setting out to describe the marks of such a state.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
verses.tr: The divine says: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom.
verses.angle: Yada marks the turning point to wisdom
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asked what a steady person looks like. Krishna answers by pointing to the exact moment this change happens. Listen for the word that marks this inner turning point.

body.text: The divine says: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom. This verse answers Arjuna's question by showing the exact moment wisdom begins. The word yada, when, marks the inner turning point. When all desires are released, the person is no longer driven by the mind, but satisfied by the self. Krishna then lists the outer marks of this state: the sage is unshaken by sorrow and free from craving in joy.

verses.tr: The steady-minded sage is unshaken by sorrow, free from craving in joy, and beyond attachment, fear, and anger.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers Arjuna's question by describing the outward behavior of a steady-minded person. Listen for the three states he names.

body.text: The steady-minded sage is unshaken by sorrow, free from craving in joy, and beyond attachment, fear, and anger. Krishna lists three poisons that a steady person has left behind: attachment, fear, and anger. These three are named together as one single condition of being, gone beyond. Krishna then asks what such a steady person looks like when they speak, and next verse describes their behavior.

verses.sa: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.tr: One who feels no clinging anywhere, and neither rejoices nor hates when good or bad comes, has steady wisdom.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been describing steady wisdom, and now he points to a specific reaction that marks it. Listen for the two things this person does not do when good or bad happens.

body.text: One who feels no clinging anywhere, and neither rejoices nor hates when good or bad comes, has steady wisdom. The verb abhinandati means to rejoice or welcome. Krishna says the person of steady wisdom does not abhinandati when good fortune comes, because they do not cling to the pleasant. Krishna now shifts from the inside feeling to the outside action, comparing the senses to a tortoise withdrawing its limbs.

verses.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.tr: When this one draws the senses fully back from sense-objects, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs, wisdom is steady.
verses.angle: the tortoise image of drawing senses inward
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has been describing a mind that no longer wavers. Now he gives a picture of how that steadiness is held.

body.text: When this one draws the senses fully back from sense-objects, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs, wisdom is steady. The verse is built on one image, that of a tortoise, and one result, steadfast wisdom. The tortoise draws in its limbs from all sides, and the wise person does the same with the senses, pulling them back from their objects. Krishna warns that even when objects fall away, the taste for them may remain, a danger the self-denying person must face.

verses.sa: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: Objects fall away from the self-denying person, but the taste for them remains. For the one who has seen the supreme reality, even that taste falls away.
verses.angle: rasah: the taste left behind by suppression
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown the tortoise method, but he now warns that even this is not enough. Listen for the inner taste that survives.

body.text: Objects fall away from the self-denying person, but the taste for them remains. For the one who has seen the supreme reality, even that taste falls away. The verse hinges on rasah, the taste, which remains when the objects disappear. Krishna says that for the embodied one who has not seen the supreme, this taste does not turn away. Krishna now adds that even a wise person's mind can be pulled away by turbulent senses.

verses.sa: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
verses.tr: Even for a wise person who strives, the turbulent senses can forcibly carry away the mind.
verses.angle: Pramathini: the senses that forcibly drag the mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that even a wise person can be dragged off course by restless senses. Listen to the force of that word.

body.text: Even for a wise person who strives, the turbulent senses can forcibly carry away the mind. The word pramathini, meaning restless or turbulent, is used for the senses. They do not just tempt the body; they forcibly drag the mind, even from a wise person who is actively trying to control them. Krishna then gives the remedy for this very struggle: restraining the senses and fixing the mind on the divine.

verses.sa: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.tr: Having restrained all the senses, the disciplined one should sit devoted to Me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly established.
verses.angle: matparah, devoted to me, makes restraint firm
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from the problem of the senses to the solution. He tells Arjuna to hold them in check and stay focused on the divine.

body.text: Having restrained all the senses, the disciplined one should sit devoted to Me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly established. Krishna does not ask Arjuna to control the senses by force alone. The word matparah, devoted to Me, shows that restraint becomes firm only when the mind is turned toward the divine. Krishna warns that even thinking about sense objects creates attachment, which can lead to anger.

verses.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
verses.tr: Thinking about sense objects creates attachment to them. Attachment gives rise to desire; desire gives rise to anger.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the first step in a chain of ruin. Listen for the word that opens the door to attachment.

body.text: Thinking about sense objects creates attachment to them. Attachment gives rise to desire; desire gives rise to anger. The verse opens with dhyayatah, while thinking. The mind does not need to act on the object yet; simply dwelling on it is enough to plant the seed of attachment. From that attachment, desire is born, and from desire, anger arises.

verses.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.tr: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, loss of discernment; from loss of discernment, ruin.
verses.angle: A path of ruin from anger
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is answering Arjuna's question about what destroys a person. Listen for the chain of ruin that starts with a single emotion.

body.text: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, loss of discernment; from loss of discernment, ruin. Krishna traces a path from anger to ruin, showing how the mind collapses from the outside in. The next verse shows the disciplined person who avoids this collapse by keeping the senses under control.

verses.tr: The disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control and free from attraction and aversion, attains serenity.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna turns from the ruin of anger to the steadiness of the disciplined person. Listen to the condition of the one who moves through the world.

body.text: The disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control and free from attraction and aversion, attains serenity. The disciplined person, the vidheyatma, keeps the senses under the control of the inner self. This inner alignment is what allows serenity to arise. Krishna now shows how this inner clarity brings an end to suffering and steadies the mind completely.

verses.sa: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
verses.tr: In inner clarity, all suffering falls away. For one whose mind is clear, understanding settles quickly.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: When the mind grows still, what falls away first? Listen to how Krishna answers that.

body.text: In inner clarity, all suffering falls away. For one whose mind is clear, understanding settles quickly. The word prasade means in clarity, and it is here that all sorrow ends for this one, because a clear mind quickly settles into understanding. Krishna then turns the chain around, showing that without peace there is no happiness at all.

verses.sa: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
verses.tr: A restless mind has no steady discernment, no steady purpose, no peace, and without peace, no happiness.
verses.angle: The chain of loss from a restless mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the total loss of a mind ruled by restless senses. Listen to the exact chain of what disappears.

body.text: A restless mind has no steady discernment, no steady purpose, no peace, and without peace, no happiness. Krishna builds a chain of loss: first steady discernment, then steady purpose, then peace, and finally happiness. Each loss depends on the one before it. One wandering sense is enough to wash away the mind's judgment, just as a wind sweeps a boat on water.
